title: MAHL: Multi-Agent LLM-Guided Hierarchical Chiplet Design with Adaptive Debugging
evidence_span: MAHL is a hierarchical LLM-based chiplet design framework with six collaborating agents for AI-to-hardware mapping, hierarchical description generation, retrieval-augmented code generation, Diverseflow validation, adaptive debugging, and multi-granularity design-space exploration. It reports Pass@5 improvement from 0 to 0.72 for real-world chiplet design in a best-case comparison and comparable or superior PPA to CLARIE under some objectives.
problem: Flat LLM-driven chiplet design has high validation cost and imprecise parameter optimization for complex hierarchical 2.5D systems.
method_or_artifact: Six-agent hierarchical workflow combining AI-hardware parsing, structured module descriptions, retrieval-augmented RTL generation, tool-based validation/debugging, multi-granularity design-space exploration, and physical-layout configuration.
workload_or_benchmark: Simple RTL and real-world AI chiplet-design tasks; PPA objectives and Pass@5 generation accuracy are evaluated against conventional LLMs and CLARIE.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 2.5D chiplet designs with AI workloads, RTL generation, synthesis/validation, and OpenROAD-like physical configuration; exact chiplet architectures, PPA flow, and design constraints require full-paper review.
metrics: real-world chiplet-design Pass@5 from 0 to 0.72 in reported best-case comparison
comparable or superior PPA to CLARIE under selected objectives
limits: The preprint evidence does not establish average-case Pass@5, design-suite breadth, prompt/model costs, physical-flow reproducibility, or fairness of the CLARIE comparison; target edition remains 2026 while paper analysis uses the 2025 fallback corpus.

title: VeriOpt: PPA-Aware High-Quality Verilog Generation via Multi-Role LLMs
evidence_span: VeriOpt structures LLM interaction into Planner, Programmer, Reviewer, and Evaluator roles and feeds synthesis reports and timing diagrams back into PPA-aware prompting. The preprint reports up to 88% power reduction, 76% area reduction, 73% timing-closure improvement versus baseline LLM-generated RTL, and 86% functional-evaluation success.
problem: LLM-generated Verilog often targets functional correctness while neglecting power, performance, and area constraints required for practical hardware.
method_or_artifact: Multi-role prompting and iterative PPA-aware optimization loop that combines planning, code generation, review, synthesis feedback, and evaluation.
workload_or_benchmark: Synthesizable Verilog generation evaluated for functional correctness and PPA using industry-standard EDA tools; exact design suite and technology conditions require paper review.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: RTL synthesis and timing/power/area evaluation with industry-standard EDA tools; process node, constraints, synthesis settings, and baseline prompts are not specified in the abstract.
limits: The preprint abstract reports maximum gains without design-by-design distributions, model details, prompt cost, EDA settings, or leakage controls; PPA claims require full-paper and artifact verification.

title: NeuroPDE: A Neuromorphic PDE Solver Based on Spintronic and Ferroelectric Devices
evidence_span: NeuroPDE uses probabilistic spin neurons to emulate random walks and non-volatile ferroelectric synapses for continuous weights in a neuromorphic PDE solver. For diffusion equations it reports variance below 1e-2 against analytical solutions, 3.48x–315x execution-time speedup, and 2.7x–29.8x energy advantage over advanced CMOS-based neuromorphic chips.
problem: Conventional von Neumann hardware lacks hardware-intrinsic randomness, limiting the performance of Monte Carlo and random-walk PDE solvers.
method_or_artifact: Neuromorphic architecture using stochastic spin neurons for probabilistic transmission and ferroelectric synapses for continuous non-volatile weights.
workload_or_benchmark: Diffusion-equation PDE solving with comparison against analytical solutions and CMOS-based neuromorphic-chip baselines.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Emerging spintronic and ferroelectric devices with physical stochasticity and non-volatile analog weight storage; device models, variability, conversion, and fabrication assumptions require full-paper review.
limits: The preprint abstract does not expose PDE suite breadth, device-area and conversion costs, process assumptions, precision, or how CMOS baselines are normalized; ranges require paper-level verification.
